questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 10 AM and 11 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 165 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **hour hand** covers 360° in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 hour = 360 / 12 = 30°

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 minute = 30 / 60 = 0.5°

The **minute hand** covers 360° in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered by the **minute hand** in 1 minute = 360 / 60 = 6°

__Calculation:__

The given time is between **10 AM** and **11 AM**. Let the time be **10:M**.

Position of the **hour hand** at 10:M (taking 12:00 as 0°):

Angle = (10 × 30°) + (M × 0.5°) = 300° + 0.5M

Position of the **minute hand** at 10:M:

Angle = M × 6° = 6M

The absolute difference between these angles is given as **165 degrees**:

| (300 + 0.5M) − 6M | = 165

| 300 − 5.5M | = 165

**Case 1:**

300 − 5.5M = 165

5.5M = 300 − 165

5.5M = 135

M = 135 / 5.5 = 270 / 11

M ≈ 24.545

Rounding to the nearest whole number, M ≈ **25 minutes**.

**Case 2:**

300 − 5.5M = −165

5.5M = 300 + 165

5.5M = 465

M = 465 / 5.5 ≈ 84.54 (This exceeds 60 minutes, so it falls outside the 10 AM to 11 AM range).

Therefore, the time is approximately **10:25 AM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle θ between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by:

θ = |30H - {11 over 2}M|

Here, H = 10 and θ = 165°.

165 = |30 × 10 − 5.5M|

165 = |300 − 5.5M|

135 = 5.5M

M = 135 / 5.5 ≈ 24.54

Hence, the approximate time is **10:25 AM**.

The correct answer is **10:25**.

questions.question: A watch is 5 minutes slow at 12 AM. It gains 10 seconds every hour. When will it show the correct time (in AM) again?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The watch is **5 minutes slow** at 12:00 AM.

It gains **10 seconds every hour**.

**Calculation:**

Initial loss = 5 minutes = 300 seconds

Gain per hour = 10 seconds

Time required to recover 300 seconds = 300 ÷ 10 = 30 hours

30 hours after 12:00 AM = 6:00 AM (next day)

Since the question asks **in AM**, the watch will show the correct time again at **6:00 AM**.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**

questions.question: The principal nitrogenous waste products excreted by human kidneys are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urea and uric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human body generates nitrogenous waste primarily from the metabolism of **proteins** and **nucleic acids**.
 
• **Ammonia** is the immediate byproduct of protein deamination, which is highly toxic; the **liver** converts it into **urea** through the **Ornithine cycle** (also known as the **Urea cycle**) to facilitate safe transport in the blood.
 
• **Urea** constitutes the largest portion of nitrogenous waste in human urine, and humans are therefore classified as **ureotelic** organisms.
 
• **Uric acid** is a nitrogenous byproduct formed during the catabolism of **purines**, which are essential components of nucleotides like **adenine** and **guanine** found in DNA and RNA.
 
• The **kidneys** serve as the primary organ for **osmoregulation** and excretion, where **nephrons** perform **ultrafiltration** to separate these nitrogenous wastes from the bloodstream for elimination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon dioxide and oxygen**:

 
 
• **Carbon dioxide** is a byproduct of **cellular respiration** but is primarily excreted via the **lungs** through expiration.
 
• **Oxygen** is an essential gas required for **aerobic respiration** and is not a waste product.
 
 
 
• **Amino acids and glucose**:
 
 
• These are vital nutrients; in healthy individuals, the **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)** of the kidney reabsorbs nearly 100% of **glucose** and **amino acids** back into the blood.
 
 
 
• **Fatty acids and glycerol**:
 
 
• These are products of **lipid digestion** and are used for **energy production** or stored in **adipose tissues** rather than being excreted as nitrogenous wastes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of reducing in waste management?

options.text: Using a paint bucket multiple times
Switching from plastic bags to jute bags
Throwing aluminium cans in the trash

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Switching from plastic bags to jute bags**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reduce** is the most prioritized component of the **waste management hierarchy** (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle), focusing on **waste prevention** by minimizing the amount of material used at the source.
 
• Switching from plastic bags to **jute bags** is a primary example of reduction because it eliminates the need for multiple **single-use plastic bags** that would otherwise end up in **landfills** or oceans.
 
• **Plastics** are derived from **petroleum products** and are **non-biodegradable**, often persisting in the environment for hundreds of years, whereas **jute** is a **natural fiber** that is **biodegradable** and **sustainable**.
 
• By choosing a long-lasting, **reusable jute bag**, a consumer effectively **reduces** the demand for plastic production and the subsequent generation of plastic waste, addressing the problem of **environmental pollution** at its origin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reuse**:

 
 
• Using a **paint bucket multiple times** is classified as **reusing** because the item is utilized repeatedly for the same or a new purpose without being processed into a new raw material.
 
 
 
• **Recycle**:
 
 
• **Recycling old newspapers** involves collecting waste paper and processing it back into **pulp** to manufacture new paper products, which helps in saving **trees** and **energy** compared to virgin production.
 
 
 
• **Waste Disposal**:
 
 
• Throwing items like **aluminium cans** in the trash is not a management strategy but a form of **disposal**; however, aluminium is 100% **recyclable** and should ideally be diverted from the waste stream.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**:
 
 
• Effective **source reduction** conserves **natural resources**, reduces **greenhouse gas emissions**, and saves **energy** required for the extraction and manufacturing of new products.

questions.question: Which architectural element is used in Rajput cenotaphs and memorials?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhatri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhatris** are elevated, dome-shaped pavilions that serve as **cenotaphs** or memorials in Indian architecture, particularly prominent in **Rajput** and **Maratha** styles.
 
• The term is derived from the Sanskrit word for **umbrella**, symbolizing protection, pride, and honor bestowed upon the deceased.
 
• These structures are typically built at the **cremation sites** of royalty and noblemen, serving as a lasting tribute rather than a tomb, as **Hinduism** generally practices cremation.
 
• Architecturally, they consist of a **raised plinth** (Jagati) supporting several **pillars**, which in turn support a central dome or multiple smaller domes often decorated with **inverted lotus** motifs.
 
• Famous examples in **Rajasthan** include the **Royal Gaitor** in Jaipur, the **Ahar Cenotaphs** in Udaipur, and the **Bada Bagh** in Jaisalmer, showcasing intricate **sandstone** and **marble** carvings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garbhagriha**:

 
 
• Refers to the **sanctum sanctorum** or the innermost chamber of a Hindu temple.
 
• It houses the **primary deity** and is usually a small, unadorned square room designed for focused worship.
 
 
 
• **Stepwell**:
 
 
• Locally known as **Baori**, **Bawdi**, or **Vav**, these are deep wells with a flight of steps leading to the water level.
 
• They were essential for **water management** and social gatherings in the arid regions of **Western India**.
 
 
 
• **Gopuram**:
 
 
• A monumental, ornate **entrance tower** characteristic of **Dravidian architecture**.
 
• These are found predominantly in **South Indian** temple complexes, often towering over the main shrine.

questions.question: On the basis of function, which of the following is not a type of animal tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vascular tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epithelial tissue** consists of cells that form a continuous sheet to cover the external body surfaces and line the internal organs and cavities for protection and secretion. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Connective tissue** is responsible for binding, supporting, and packing various organs of the body, and it includes specialized forms like **bone**, **cartilage**, and **blood**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Muscular tissue** is made up of elongated cells called **muscle fibers** that contain contractile proteins, enabling the body to perform movement and locomotion. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Vascular tissue** is a specialized conducting tissue found in **plants**, consisting of **Xylem** and **Phloem**, which facilitate the transport of water and nutrients. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• In animals, the components of the **circulatory system** (veins, arteries, and blood) are classified under **epithelial** and **connective tissues** rather than being labeled as a separate 'vascular tissue' category in histology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Animal Tissues**:

 
 
• **Nervous Tissue**: Composed of **neurons** that receive and transmit electrochemical impulses, primarily located in the **brain** and **spinal cord**.
 
• **Muscular Tissue Subtypes**: Includes **Skeletal** (striated/voluntary), **Smooth** (non-striated/involuntary), and **Cardiac** (heart muscles).
 
• **Epithelial Subtypes**: Categorized as **Squamous**, **Cuboidal**, or **Columnar** based on cell shape.
 
 
 
• **Plant Vascular System**:
 
 
• **Xylem**: Responsible for the unidirectional transport of **water** and **dissolved minerals** from roots to leaves.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about decomposers?

__
 
• **Decomposers** are organisms, primarily **bacteria** and **fungi**, that break down dead or decaying organic matter, including animal remains and leaf litter.
 
• The biological process of **decomposition** involves the conversion of complex organic substances into simpler **inorganic matter** such as carbon dioxide, water, and nutrients.
 
• By breaking down the **detritus**, these organisms release essential chemical elements like **nitrogen**, **phosphorus**, and **potassium** back into the ecosystem.
 
• These recycled nutrients are absorbed by the **soil**, where they become available for uptake by **primary producers** (plants) to sustain new growth.
 
• This function is critical for maintaining **ecological balance** and completing the **nutrient cycle**, ensuring that life-sustaining minerals are not permanently lost to the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Autotrophic Organisms**:

 
 
• These are **producers**, such as green plants and algae, that synthesize their own food using **sunlight** (photosynthesis) or chemical energy (chemosynthesis).
 
• **Decomposers** are actually **heterotrophic**, specifically **saprotrophs**, because they rely on external organic sources for energy.
 
 
 
• **Consumers and Predators**:
 
 
• Organisms that **eat live animals** are known as **carnivores** or predators, occupying higher **trophic levels** in the food web.
 
• **Scavengers** like vultures initiate the breakdown of large carcasses, but only **decomposers** finish the process at a molecular level.
 
 
 
• **Plant Nutrition**:
 
 
• While decomposers provide the **raw inorganic minerals**, plants produce their own 'food' (glucose) via the **chloroplasts** in their leaves.

questions.question: What is the primary function of villi in the small intestine in humans?

options.text: To increase the surface area for absorption

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To increase the surface area for absorption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Villi** are tiny, finger-like projections that line the inner walls of the **small intestine** in the human digestive system.
 
• The primary function of these structures is to dramatically increase the **surface area** available for the absorption of digested food molecules into the bloodstream.
 
• Increased surface area is critical because the rate of **nutrient absorption** is directly proportional to the surface area in contact with the **chyme** (partially digested food).
 
• Each villus contains a network of **blood capillaries** and a central lymphatic vessel known as a **lacteal**, which facilitate the immediate transport of nutrients.
 
• Without villi, the small intestine would need to be considerably longer to absorb the same amount of **glucose**, **amino acids**, and **fatty acids** required by the body.
 
• The epithelial cells covering the villi further possess **microvilli**, which together create a **brush border**, increasing the absorptive surface area by nearly 600 times compared to a flat surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lacteals**:

 
 
• These are specialized **lymphatic capillaries** located inside each villus.
 
• They are responsible for absorbing **dietary fats** and fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K) that are too large to enter blood capillaries directly.
 
 
 
• **Digestive Enzymes**:
 
 
• While the **pancreas** and **stomach** secrete major enzymes, the **brush border** of the villi also produces enzymes like **maltase**, **sucrase**, and **lactase** to finalize the digestion of carbohydrates.
 
 
 
• **Neutralizing Stomach Acid**:
 
 
• This process is primarily handled by **bicarbonate ions** released from the **pancreas** into the **duodenum**, rather than by the villi themselves.
 
 
 
• **Food Breakdown**:
 
 
• Mechanical breakdown occurs through **mastication** in the mouth and **peristalsis** in the stomach; villi only handle the end-stage absorption of the broken-down molecules.

• The **first stage** (S1) was the largest, generating a maximum thrust of **43 tonnes** to lift the vehicle off the launch pad.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a side effect of Narcotics in sports?

• **Narcotics**, specifically **opioid analgesics** such as **morphine**, **methadone**, and **pethidine**, act directly on the **central nervous system** to alleviate intense pain. A significant physiological side effect of these substances is the depression of the **autonomic nervous system**, which leads to **bradycardia** (a notable **decrease in heart rate**) and reduced **blood pressure**. **Hence, statement I is correct.**
 
• The ingestion of narcotics frequently stimulates the **chemoreceptor trigger zone** located in the **medulla oblongata** of the brain. This stimulation, combined with the irritation of the **gastrointestinal tract**, commonly results in symptoms of **nausea** and **vomiting**. These reactions are among the most prevalent acute adverse effects reported by individuals using these substances. **Hence, statement II is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narcotics** are strictly monitored and banned in-competition by the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** because they allow athletes to perform beyond their natural pain threshold, risking severe injury.

 
 
• **Respiratory Depression**: The most severe risk involves a decrease in the **respiratory drive**, which can lead to inadequate **oxygenation** of the blood and potentially fatal outcomes.
 
• **Impaired Coordination**: These substances cause **drowsiness**, loss of **mental focus**, and impaired **physical balance**, which can lead to accidents during athletic activities.
 
• **Addiction and Tolerance**: Long-term use often results in **physical dependence** and **addiction**, necessitating higher doses to achieve the same analgesic effect.
 
• **Gastrointestinal Issues**: Beyond vomiting, narcotics are notorious for causing chronic **constipation** by slowing down the **motility** of the digestive system.

questions.question: 91 - 33 + 28 + 47 ÷ 1 + (24 of 1) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **BODMAS** rule to prioritize operations: **Bracket/Of** → **Division** → **Addition** → **Subtraction**.

Solve **Of** and **Division** first: (24 of 1) = 24 and 47 ÷ 1 = 47.

The expression becomes: 91 − 33 + 28 + 47 + 24.

Group positive values: (91 + 28 + 47 + 24) − 33 = 190 − 33 = 157.

**∴ The correct answer is 157.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

91 − 33 + 28 + 47 ÷ 1 + (24 of 1)

**Formula Used:**

The **BODMAS** rule: **B**rackets, **O**f, **D**ivision, **M**ultiplication, **A**ddition, and **S**ubtraction.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 91 − 33 + 28 + 47 ÷ 1 + 24 (Solving **Of/Bracket**: 24 × 1 = 24)

⇒ 91 − 33 + 28 + 47 + 24 (Solving **Division**: 47 ÷ 1 = 47)

⇒ 58 + 28 + 47 + 24 (Solving **Subtraction**: 91 − 33 = 58)

⇒ 86 + 47 + 24 (Solving **Addition**: 58 + 28 = 86)

⇒ 133 + 24 = 157

**∴ The correct answer is 157.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Standard order for solving mathematical expressions: **Brackets** (), **Of** (multiplication), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), **Subtraction** (−).

VBODMAS Rule

An extension where **V** stands for **Vinculum** (bar bracket), which is solved even before standard brackets.

Operation of Of

In mathematical simplification, the term **of** represents multiplication but holds higher precedence than division and standard multiplication.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve **Division** and **Multiplication**: 36 ÷ 6 = 6 and 42 × 1 = 42.

Resulting expression: 93 − 6 + 29 + 42 − 14 + 18.

Combine all positive and negative values: (93 + 29 + 42 + 18) − (6 + 14) = 182 − 20 = 162.

∴ The correct answer is 162.</strong&g

questions.question: A jar contains a mixture of 36 litres in the ratio of 2:1:1 of alcohol, acid, and water. 12 litres are drawn out and replaced with acid. What is the new ratio?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total volume is 36 litres and 12 litres are removed, which is 1/3 of the total.

Remaining volume = 24 litres. Ratio 2:1:1 remains constant in the residual mixture.

In 24 L: Alcohol = 12 L, Acid = 6 L, Water = 6 L.

Add 12 L acid: Alcohol = 12 L, Acid = 18 L, Water = 6 L.

New ratio = 12 : 18 : 6 ⇒ 2 : 3 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2:3:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial volume = 36 litres, Ratio = 2:1:1, Drawn out = 12 litres, Replaced with Acid.

**Formula:** Component quantity = (Ratio part ÷ Total parts) × Total volume

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6cdb1c5f5f76e4f89e2b34151fe4a7da1390da180b4edb6b2af6a70933f9024.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ **Total parts** = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 units

⇒ **Initial quantities:** Alcohol = (2/4) × 36 = 18 L, Acid = (1/4) × 36 = 9 L, Water = (1/4) × 36 = 9 L.

⇒ When 12 L mixture is removed, **Remaining volume** = 36 − 12 = 24 L.

⇒ **Remaining quantities (Ratio 2:1:1):** Alcohol = (2/4) × 24 = 12 L, Acid = (1/4) × 24 = 6 L, Water = (1/4) × 24 = 6 L.

⇒ 12 L **Acid is added** to the mixture.

⇒ **New quantities:** Alcohol = 12 L, Acid = 6 + 12 = 18 L, Water = 6 L.

⇒ **New Ratio** = 12 : 18 : 6 = 2 : 3 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2:3:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixture Replacement Rule

When a portion of a **mixture** is removed, the **ratio** of components in the remaining mixture and the portion removed remains the same as the initial ratio.

Final Ratio Calculation

The final quantity of a component after removal and replacement can be found by adding the added quantity to its residual quantity: Qfᵢₙₐₗ = Qᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ − Qᵣₑₘₒvₑd + Qₐddₑd.

Ratio Simplification

A ratio a : b : c can be simplified by dividing all terms by their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** to represent it in the simplest form.

questions.question: If 5 men or 8 women can do a piece of work in 20 days, find how long it will take 10 men and 4 women to complete the same work together.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **And/Or** formula: **Time** = **Days** ÷ [(**Mₐₙd** ÷ **Mₒᵣ**) + (**Wₐₙd** ÷ **Wₒᵣ**)]

⇒ **Time** = 20 ÷ [(10 ÷ 5) + (4 ÷ 8)]

⇒ **Time** = 20 ÷ [2 + 0.5] = 20 ÷ 2.5 = 8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **5 men** or **8 women** complete the work in **20 days**.

**Efficiency:** Since 5M = 8W, the ratio of **Efficiency** (M:W) = 8:5 (1 Man = 8 units/day, 1 Woman = 5 units/day).

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **5 Men**
 20
 800
 5 × 8 = 40
 
 

 **10 Men** + **4 Women**
 8
 10(8) + 4(5) = 100
 
 

⇒ **Total Work** = **Efficiency** × **Time** = (5 × 8) × 20 = 800 units.

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** of **10 men** and **4 women** = 10(8) + 4(5) = 80 + 20 = 100 units/day.

⇒ **Time Taken** = **Total Work** ÷ **Combined Efficiency** = 800 ÷ 100 = 8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

For work-related problems, M₁ × D₁ × H₁ ÷ W₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ ÷ W₂, where M is **manpower**, D is **days**, H is **hours**, and W is **work**.

Pipes and Cisterns

The same **efficiency** logic applies here; inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet (leakage) pipes have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

**Wages** are always distributed in the ratio of the **work done** by each person, which is (Efficiency × Time).

questions.question: Which of the following options will have sum as (5/6)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check which **fraction** pair has a cross-product **sum** that equals the target **numerator** (5) when using the common **denominator** (6).

For 1/3 + 1/2: Cross-multiply → (1 × 2) + (1 × 3) = 2 + 3 = 5.

Common denominator: 3 × 2 = 6.

The resulting **fraction** is 5/6, which matches the target.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3 + 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Target **sum** = 5/6.

**Formula Used:** To add **unlike fractions**, use the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the **denominators**: a/b + c/d = (ad + bc) / bd.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13877520b13ac6d090dda4d0cb97d54ce44318d88dc9669f74df12f7089686a2.png] 

⇒ Denominators of the selected option are 3 and 2.

⇒ **LCM** of 3 and 2 = 6.

⇒ Convert 1/3 to an **equivalent fraction**: (1 × 2) / (3 × 2) = 2/6.

⇒ Convert 1/2 to an **equivalent fraction**: (1 × 3) / (2 × 3) = 3/6.

⇒ Add the **numerators**: 2/6 + 3/6 = (2 + 3) / 6 = 5/6.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3 + 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition of Unlike Fractions

To add fractions with different **denominators**, they must first be converted into **like fractions** by finding the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

Equivalent Fractions

Multiplying both the **numerator** and the **denominator** by the same non-zero number creates an **equivalent fraction** (e.g., 1/2 = 3/6).

Unit Fractions

A **fraction** where the **numerator** is 1 is called a **unit fraction**. The sum of two **unit fractions** 1/x + 1/y is always (x + y) / (x × y).

questions.question: The product of the three consecutive odd numbers is 105. Which is the smallest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perform prime **factorization** of 105: 105 = 3 × 5 × 7.

Observe that 3, 5, and 7 are **consecutive odd numbers**.

The **smallest** number in the sequence 3, 5, 7 is 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The product of three **consecutive odd numbers** is 105.

**Method:** Algebraic representation and product estimation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12f234d38a5f69073c52274bc490a4941b80a21a26b059ba33175549d7a4cc15.png] 

⇒ Let the three consecutive odd numbers be x, (x + 2), and (x + 4).

⇒ x × (x + 2) × (x + 4) = 105

⇒ Since the product is 105 (ends in 5), one of the odd numbers must be **5**.

⇒ Testing the set around 5: 3 × 5 × 7 = 105.

⇒ The condition is satisfied for numbers 3, 5, and 7.

⇒ Smallest number = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Odd Numbers

Numbers that follow each other by a constant difference of 2. They can be represented as (2n−1), (2n+1), (2n+3) etc.

Properties of Product

If the product of three consecutive numbers (x−d), x, (x+d) is given, the middle term is approximately the **cube root** of the product.

Divisibility Rule of 5

Any integer ending in 5 or 0 is divisible by 5. In a product of odd numbers ending in 5, at least one factor must be a multiple of 5.

questions.question: The sum of the three consecutive even numbers is 42. What is the product of the smallest and the largest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an odd number of **consecutive even numbers**, the **middle number** is always equal to the average.

**Average** = 42 ÷ 3 = 14

The three numbers are: 14 − 2, 14, 14 + 2 ⇒ **12, 14, 16**

**Product** of smallest and largest = 12 × 16 = 192

**∴ The correct answer is 192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of **three consecutive even numbers** is 42.

Let the three consecutive even numbers be **x − 2**, **x**, and **x + 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/027fbebcced570edd6b3aa9edf070a3eef8340016b8cc008cc357b24f28d1133.png] 

⇒ (x − 2) + x + (x + 2) = 42

⇒ 3x = 42

⇒ x = 42 ÷ 3 = 14

⇒ **Smallest number** = x − 2 = 14 − 2 = 12

⇒ **Largest number** = x + 2 = 14 + 2 = 16

⇒ **Required Product** = 12 × 16 = 192

**∴ The correct answer is 192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Even Numbers

Even numbers that follow each other in order with a constant difference of 2. Example: 2n, 2n+2, 2n+4.

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Property

The average of a set of numbers in AP is exactly the middle term if the number of terms is odd.

Sum of first n even numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive even numbers starting from 2 is given by the formula n(n + 1).

⇒ **d**² = 162

⇒ **d** = √162 = 9√2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 9√2 cm.**

**Given:** Area of the square = 81 cm².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a3f90776c3ff36682b161f8f4305c51d666a1028db89ae75f1aa5d669644525.png] 

⇒ **a**² = 81

⇒ **a** = √81 = 9 cm

⇒ **Diagonal** = a × √2

Perimeter of a Square

Pythagoras Theorem in Square

The diagonal divides the square into two right-angled triangles. **d**² = a² + a² = 2a², which leads to d = a√2.

Incircle and Circumcircle

Radius of **incircle** = a/2. Radius of **circumcircle** = d/2 = a/√2.

Perimeter of a Rectangle

Diagonal of a Rectangle

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence of numbers where the difference between consecutive terms is constant. The **nth term** is given by aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.

Sum of First 'n' Natural Numbers

Sum of 'n' terms of an AP

questions.question: In a match, average of runs scored by 7 players is 50. Runs scored by first 6 players are 110, 40, 29, 56, 30 and 52. How many players scored less than the 7th player?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net deviation from the **average (50)** must be **zero**.

Deviations: (110−50) + (40−50) + (29−50) + (56−50) + (30−50) + (52−50) = +60 − 10 − 21 + 6 − 20 + 2 = **+17**.

To balance, the **7th player** deviation must be **−17** ⇒ 50 − 17 = **33 runs**.

Comparing **33** with other scores: only **29** and **30** are less than 33.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 players.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of **7 players** = 50 runs

Runs of **6 players** = 110, 40, 29, 56, 30, 52

**Formula Used:**

Total value = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24bc9972bc324d71c87e76da99ac593933466148eef0bf95c5d1352b79ccc136.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total runs of **7 players** = 50 × 7 = 350

⇒ Sum of runs of **first 6 players** = 110 + 40 + 29 + 56 + 30 + 52 = 317

⇒ Runs of **7th player** = 350 − 317 = 33

⇒ Scores lower than **33** from the given list: 29 and 30.

⇒ Number of such players = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 players.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The average or mean is calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations. Formula: Mean = (Σxᵢ) / n.

Deviation Property

The sum of deviations of a set of values from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This is a very useful property for finding missing values in a series.

If each observation is increased or decreased by a constant value 'k', the new average will also increase or decrease by 'k'.

questions.question: Average of 14 numbers is 'm'. Average of 5 numbers among them is 43. Average of the remaining numbers is 57. What is the value of 'm'?

Assume the base **average** is 43.

Remaining 9 **numbers** have a surplus of (57 − 43) = 14 each.

Total surplus = 9 × 14 = 126.

Net increase in **average** = Total surplus ÷ Total **numbers** = 126 ÷ 14 = 9.

Required value m = 43 + 9 = 52.

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Total sum of 14 **numbers** = 14 × m

⇒ 14 × m = 728

⇒ m = 728 ÷ 14

⇒ m = 52

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

questions.question: When 11 percent of a number is added to 117, then the result is 24 percent of that number. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between the two **percentages** given is 24% − 11% = **13%**.

According to the question, this 13% gap is equal to the value **117**.

⇒ 13% → 117

⇒ 1% → 117 ÷ 13 = 9

⇒ 100% (The number) → 9 × 100 = **900**

**∴ The correct answer is 900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Addition value = **117**

First percentage = **11%**

Number = (Value × 100) ÷ (Percentage Difference)

**Calculations:**

Let the **number** be x.

⇒ (11/100) × x + 117 = (24/100) × x

⇒ 117 = (24x/100) − (11x/100)

⇒ 117 = 13x / 100

⇒ x = (117 × 100) ÷ 13

⇒ x = 9 × 100

⇒ x = **900**

**∴ The correct answer is 900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change
